utterances.text: -- you indicate that the Assembly accepts the appointment of Mr. Jovan Cizmovic as the coordinator of the governments of the Serbian autonomous regions. And then on the following page in English and at --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. It's really not on page 34. I really need to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your page -- sorry, Mr. Krajisnik, I understand the confusion. Your page is probably 5132. Just --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And then on the subsequent page, there's simply a list of the members of the Council of Ministers, including Jovan Cizmovic, coordinator of activities of the governments of the Serbian autonomous regions.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correct. Number 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I think you indicate at page 36, the following page, just after the list of those persons and after Mr. Bjelosevic, and Mr. Saric, and Mr. Knezevic speak, you explain, again at the bottom of page 36 of the English and page 5136 of your version, Mr. Krajisnik, that the Council of Ministers should be a kind of executive body of the Serbian Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in connection with our earlier discussion you'll see if you just read down slight --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't find it. What I meant to say was that you are right. It was, indeed, the function, the purpose, of the ministerial council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And just -- in connection with our earlier discussion about Mr. Stanisic, you'll see at your page SA025136, the second -- well, that first and second paragraph end at -- beginning at page 36, at the bottom of the English. "If you agree, I would like to propose that we include Mr. Mico Stanisic as well. Additionally I think we should emphasise that all appointments and dismissals, including my post in the last backbencher, excuse me my language, can be subjected to debate of an accession. This is my proposal and I would like you to accept it." So that's the -- at least one of the points in the session that reflects Mr. Stanisic's selection to the ministerial council?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An MP proposed Stanisic instead of Zepinic or instead of somebody else. I don't know. And he was on the city MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So I proposed that this should be adopted, but there were also suggestions to change a lot of other things, whereas we wanted this pattern to remain, that only people in positions in Bosnia and Herzegovina be included in the Council of Ministers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, on that same day, December 21st, you had a conversation with Dr. Karadzic about the Council of Ministers and about Mr. Cizmovic. And in that connection if we could turn to tab 59, and if we could look at the -- at the bottom of page 2 of the English and in the B/C/S, Mr. Krajisnik, at the top of 02079288.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And during that conversation you said: "But what do you ... Here, you know what? They told me that the people from Krajina are dissatisfied with that Cizmovic ... I don't know that" --

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: " All right. That's until the new year, the Serbian new year. Then we'll see." And you say: "But I don't understand this. How did the idea come up that we should coordinate this?"

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "You know what? Who will implement what we issued last night?" And you say: "This Council of Ministers." And Dr. Karadzic says: "But they can't run from municipality to municipality." Krajisnik: "Huh?" Karadzic: "They can't run from municipality to municipality and say do this or do that." Krajisnik: "But he won't run either." Karadzic: "But he must run." What was it, Mr. Krajisnik, that Mr. Cizmovic was supposed to run from municipality to municipality to ensure that "what we issued last night," as Dr. Karadzic said it, was implemented? What was he supposed to implement?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at this carefully, Karadzic says that his term of office is until the Serb new year. And it concerns a decision to form the Republic of Serb People by the Serb new year, that that should be discussed, and you will find this deadline. So we had autonomous regions and they needed to be coordinated. Plus there is other background material that is assigned. If these are instructions A and B, then it applies to the eventuality of war; it doesn't apply just to the Serb new year. I spoke to Cizmovic because the grassroots were opposed to it. He just mentioned this deadline, the Serb new year, because we said we would form the Serb republic if they go through with their independence. We discussed their decision to seek recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And we said: If you go through with this referendum concerning independence, then we'll proclaim the Serb republic, and the deadline is Serb new year.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if they don't go through with it, if they withdraw the memorandum, if they back off of their intention, that is the Muslims back off of their intention to become independent, then the state wouldn't be proclaimed, then the -- and there would be no longer any need to take the preparatory steps represented from Variant A and B because the problem, from the Serb point of view, would be solved. That's what that refers to. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not A and B. Look here. The draft decision to proclaim the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the draft that I provided on that DVD, so it was a contingency decision, saying that if Bosnia and Herzegovina is recognised as independent, then the decision comes into force. At the session itself, MPs deleted the "if" and "when." So it was formulated that the Serb republic would be proclaimed by the 13th of January because they had already decided to go through with independence. I don't dispute that the paper existed but it has nothing to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's be clear on one thing. At that point, the reference, as you pointed out, to the new year was a reference to the contingency that you describe. That is, the proclamation of the state was contingent on whether or not the Muslims move forward, which was essentially --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Please, you can find this in the documents. It says precisely: We are going forward with preparations for proclaiming a Serb republic because Muslims had already applied for recognition of independence. That was supposed to be done by the 13th of January. And the draft envisaged that our decision would only come into force if and when they get it, because they had only just applied. A and B is a contingency plan only in case of war; that's how I understood it. This was just a preparation. Please, look at it. This decision concerned only preparation, and it was promulgated on the 9th of January instead of on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, and you, both repeatedly warned people that war would come about if Bosnia -- if the Muslims in Bosnia continued to pursue their move toward independence. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I don't know how many times I've said this. The smallest child in Bosnia and Herzegovina felt that Bosnia and Herzegovina was going into war because not only a crisis had been created --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, excuse me --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but -- do you want me to answer or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I do want you to answer, and that's why I'm refocussing you on the question. Didn't Dr. Karadzic repeatedly say that war would happen if the Muslims in Bosnia continued to pursue their move toward independence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not if they continue, but if Bosnia and Herzegovina is proclaimed as an independent state, war could start and, in fact, war would start. That was the prevailing opinion. On that point, you are undoubtedly right. And it happened, people knew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question because it's not entirely clear to me. Mr. Krajisnik, it seems that Mr. Karadzic, that's at least what I read as being his suggestion, that for the implementation of what was issued last night, one would need to run from municipality to municipality and tell them: Do this, do that. That's what he suggests would be necessary for implementation. Now, please explain to me if this was about the promulgation, as you said, early January of the -- it was the promulgation of the -- let me just check --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think of the declaration of the state, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, declaration of the state. Could you tell me why you would have to run from municipality to municipality and instruct people what to do. That's not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Cizmovic was coordinator of autonomous regions, where it had been noted that many of them were not actually operating. He says he would go from municipality to municipality, and I tell him: Well, we have the ministerial council. It was elected at the Assembly. It has nothing to do with the A and B variants. And then he says: Then I won't be running anywhere either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you -- at least that's how I understand it where we are talking about the proclamation of promulgation of a declaration of a state. When I ask: What would be the purpose of running from municipality to municipality and tell the people what to do in preparation of the declaration of a state, and in your answer you focus on regionalisation and you are not talking anymore about what I ask you, that is what would be the purpose of such activity as a preparation for the declaration of a state.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, autonomous regions have a purpose. Only -- I mean, once the Serb republic is proclaimed, they are no longer necessary, and the deadline was the 13th of January. So he will work until they are established, because it was noted here that they did not actually exist for any practical purpose. I was against any efforts to coordinate on his part. What business does he have to go from Assembly to Assembly? And it says here, it is written, that the regions had not been established, and he was their coordinator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I tend to agree with your answer, if it is just to tell them that once the state had been declared that there was no need anymore for regions, but that's -- apparently is not what Mr. Karadzic has in mind. Mr. Karadzic has in mind that you have to run from municipality to municipality and to tell them what to do. From what I understand from your answer it is just waiting until whether the state will be proclaimed, yes or no, because then there is no need for them to further function anymore. But it's still unclear what exactly this "running from municipality to municipality, tell them: Do this, do that," how that could play a role in the preparation of the declaration of the state in early January.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you allow me to explain, Mr. President? Mr. Cizmovic was the coordinator for autonomous regions, and that has nothing to do with the proclamation of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not the state, according to the Cutileiro Plan. At this session there were two issues: The end of regionalisation, that's why they put him there in the first place. As for the preparations for the establishment of the Serb republic, Karadzic says: Up until the 13th of January his action will go on; after that, we don't need him because he thinks that by then the Serb republic will be proclaimed because that was the deadline. Up until that point, there should be these regions that are not functioning. Just look at the instructions. There is not a single action that he should carry through. Everybody was there at the gathering. If they received Variants A and B, why would Cizmovic have to tell them? Karadzic could have told them and he had nothing to do in the field anymore, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're now focussing on the person rather than what was, in Mr. Karadzic's view --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- needed to implement what was issued last night that would require to go from municipality to municipality and to tell them what to do. And that's still a puzzle, but let's proceed. We'll try to -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll explain, I'll explain. Just a bit more, please, Mr. President. As far as I understood it then, as far as I understand it now -- well, I don't have to explain, but I thought if it was not clear I should explain it. So I'm trying to interpret this. Mr. Karadzic said that the 13th of January was the deadline. Mr. Cizmovic was in charge of coordinating autonomous regions that had not actually started functioning yet. On the 13th of January, the Serb republic was supposed to be proclaimed. He could only work on the coordination of the unestablished autonomous regions. That was his task. Had he received a task for Variants A and B? Well, I don't know what he said to him, but this is my understanding then and this is my understanding today. So -- and I said: Let the ministerial council. Why would Cizmovic have to do that? Well, that's about it. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The same day, Mr. Krajisnik, Dr. Karadzic had a telephone conversation with Mr. Cizmovic, which we'll find at tab 60. And if we could turn to page 2 of the English and the second page of your version, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: "The most important thing now in this very moment is that those papers, those ..." And Cizmovic says: "To the realisation." Karadzic: "Right, right." Cizmovic: "Fine." Karadzic: "This is now the most import ..." Cizmovic: "The most important." Karadzic: "You have full authorisation to visit those municipalities, even those where there is no ... and all those there who are ours." Now, Mr. Krajisnik -- take a moment if you want to look at that.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just have a look at the whole conversation, just for a minute, please. Yes, please go ahead. I have read it. I have read the important parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So when Dr. Karadzic and you were talking on December 21st about implementing "what we issued last night," and having Cizmovic do it, "that's a reference to," as Dr. Karadzic says in his conversation with Mr. Cizmovic, "those papers."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says so right here. Look. This is just an announcement that we're going to proclaim the Serb republic. See? It's right after that, and it -- that's what it says here. And then he talks about Bosanska Krajina that wants to be on its own. I really don't know what other papers. Perhaps there were some papers that I was not aware of, but this is what he's saying here. I read it. Right here. I'm sorry, please have a look. "Well, no way. They will be independent but they will have to be in a unified Bosnia." He's talking about the autonomous regions. That was my understanding -- that is my understanding. I don't know. But not unified Bosnia, you know? They were afraid that there would be a unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they kept wanting to create the Bosanska Krajina into a state because they were afraid of a unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina and that they would stay there. So what papers? I don't know. Cizmovic left. He did not see Karadzic before he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, if the question --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, Mr. Prosecutor. Let me just help you. Cizmovic says:" All right. Tell me, shall we act as a shock absorber in terms of these actions of theirs for independence." See, that's what he's saying about the people of Krajina who want to create an independent republic. And Karadzic says: "Yes, yes, by all means, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, if you're raising the question of what papers we're talking about, let's turn to tab 63 in a conversation between Mr. Karadzic and Miroslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, just one moment. Sorry, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you turn to page 7 of the English and the -- and page 03244715 --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any page numbers, so do you mind if I just read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's the -- Mr. Krajisnik, you'll see very small page numbers about two-thirds of the way down each page.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. Yes, yes. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There Dr. Karadzic tells Miroslav: "No, it's not a time for science. It is time to take over real functions, real functions. This, this, and this real function and chop-chop. And there isn't any ... In the sense of that paper ... I don't know. That paper of ours, level one, level two."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's a clear reference to Variant A and B, Mr. Krajisnik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can assume that that's what it is, what I'm reading here, but the entire content here has to do with the community of municipalities, the government being established, all of that, the autonomous regions, and Karadzic is saying to take over power, in fact, not to work only on the basis of declarations. See what it says here: "We're going to do this declaratively," but it says level one, level two which is referred to in Variants A and B. I did not know about this. But he's adding the point here, "this paper," "I don't know this paper here of ours," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I make one suggestion, Your Honour. This is the second intercept that, according to the index that's been provided, has previously been exhibited. Could I invite my learned friend to read out the exhibit number when he asks the witness about the particular intercept, because otherwise we're all going to get rather confused when we come to review this in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: A very fair request, Your Honour, and I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it then that we just looked at P529, tab 376?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's right, and for the record then the tab 59, which was a conversation between the witness and Dr. Karadzic was P64A and also part of P64A and P529, tab 383.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's still a mystery what tab that would be under P64A, and we quite a large choice. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, the conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Miroslav took place shortly before the first Council of Ministers meeting on January 11th. Let's turn first, if we can, to a conversation between you and Dr. Karadzic found at tab 64 on January 10th.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: 64? The last one I have here is 63.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then we'll have to distribute tabs 64 and the ones thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, and I'd like actually, first, to turn to 65, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's a conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Cizmovic. And beginning at the first page, Mr. Krajisnik, and it will certainly be the first page of your version as well, where it begins: "Simovic called me about this tomorrow ..." Do you see that? It's about seven lines down from the top.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I found that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Cizmovic says: "Simovic called me about this tomorrow." Karadzic: "Yes." Cizmovic: "What should I do?" Karadzic: "It's better for you to be here, because executive matters will take place here" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, in the English, I read: "Simovic called me about this tomorrow." I mean, if this sentence would not end there, it would just suggest that it was something else and it was interrupted, then I have no problems. But "tomorrow," if someone calls tomorrow, I would have expected him to have called yesterday, but not today, but not tomorrow. Could we just check on the -- perhaps someone could read the -- which seems to be the -- the eighth box. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to read it, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just wondering whether you could slowly read it to see if it makes sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Simovic called me about this thing tomorrow."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The mystery is the same. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, do you understand that to mean, and I'll ask you this, that Mr. Cizmovic is referring -- is saying that Simovic called him and the subject matter of the call was something that -- this thing that's going to take place tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. For something that's going to take place tomorrow, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic says: "Yes." Cizmovic: "What should I do?" Karadzic: "It's better for you to be here, because executive matters will take place here, and I think that Leovac and Najdanovic will go over there." And then further down the page in the middle of the English on page 2 and again on page 2 of your version: "They should let them solve it by themselves," says Cizmovic. "Actually, only the mandators will be appointed here tomorrow, the mandators, formally speaking, because they must be reduced to executive council ..." Karadzic: "That's clear; that's right. Cizmovic: "... of the government. However, this sound good to them, like this ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you're reading very fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Krajisnik, if you could turn to the last page -- actually, it's the bottom of the second-to-last page, the very last comment by Dr. Karadzic on the second-to-last page of your version and the bottom of page 4 in the English. "They will be guests and you are needed here because there will be specific tasks tomorrow," says Dr. Karadzic. Now, the next day was January 11th, and as we've seen before January 11th was the first meeting of the Council of Ministers, which can be found at tab 68.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that was the case. I know that there were two meetings in January.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you and Dr. Karadzic attended both meetings, correct, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what's written here, then yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There may be a misunderstanding on my side, you see 68 it is the second meeting, not the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. It should be tab 66. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And turning to page 2 of both the English and B/C/S versions under the heading "execution of tasks resulting from the declaration of the promulgation of the republic of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina," we see first that it reflects the discussion of issues regarding the execution of tasks resulting from the declaration and that you and Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Dukic and Mr. Savic participated in the discussion alongside the members of the ministerial council. And then it indicates: "It was concluded that the priorities springing from the declaration included" --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I don't think Mr. Krajisnik's got the place, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I indicated it was page 2 of his version as well, and I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it's not on the other page. That's it. The minutes were adopted, and then the provisional rules of procedure. That's what's on the other page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I find on page 2, item 2, there's an item 2 on page 1 as well, but on page 2 you have underlined in the becoming version, which deals apparently with the -- it says: "The declaration," I take it, from the Republika Srpska -- of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You found that, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we talking about tab 68?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are talking about 66. It has been corrected.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the top of the page, the page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. I looked at 68 a few moments ago; that was the mistake. I'm so sorry. Could you tell me what the question was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Just focussing your attention to the second paragraph of item 2, "execution of tasks," which reads: "It was concluded that the priorities springing from the declaration included the defining of ethnic territory, establishment of government organs in the territory, and the economic disempowerment of the current authorities in the socialist republic of BH." And then the next paragraph states: "During discussion it was especially stressed that the ministerial council's function, and the executive organ of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina, must be taken as a starting point in charting the council's work programme." So these reflect the priority items emerging from the first session of the ministerial council held on the 11th of January, 1992. Is that right, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here and that's correct, yes, after the establishment of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, you and Dr. Karadzic had a telephone conversation prior to a meeting of the Council of Ministers, and that is found at tab 64. And on the first page of the English and the first page of the B/C/S, just slightly below the -- just slightly -- the beginning of the bottom half of the page you say to Dr. Karadzic: "And another thing, we have a Council of Ministers today. Don't know at what time. At 17 I think."

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: "Uh-huh." And you say: "Here. Then I'll manage. There's some meeting, but before that I will talk to them to get them to make some decisions and then we'll see." What -- what decisions did you want members of the ministerial council to make, that is what decisions were you referring to in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember what decisions, but I can tell you what the activity was at the time. That's probably it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you mean what generally you were focussed on at the time? Well, please go ahead, and hear -- the activity at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean what the ministerial council should do. We started engaging in activities that were envisaged by the Cutileiro Plan, as opposed to the Muslims who were working for independence. And let me just tell you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, no, let me stop you. Please, if you want to tell us about concrete activities that were underway, please do so. If I want to know why those activities were underway or what the Muslims were doing or not doing, I'll also ask you that.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't have the patience to hear me out, and that's the sentence that I wanted to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please tell us about concrete activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this time preparations started for drafting the constitution of Republika Srpska, thoughts along those lines, and so on and so forth. The constitutional commission already had talks about this and, as I said, all of this was in the context of the Cutileiro Plan, which was proven by the draft itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I'm aware of the clock, talking about concrete activities. Perhaps you should have a break for 20 minutes and -- unless this would be an unsuitable moment for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think that's a suitable moment, Your Honour. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, we'll have a short session until 25 minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, Your Honour. We have been advised.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could ask the Court and Mr. Krajisnik to turn to tab 67. That contains a conversation between Mr. Cizmovic and Dr. Karadzic on the 16th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's P529, Hanson tab 385.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 7 of the English, and that begins, Mr. Krajisnik, if you'll see again the small ERN number at the bottom third of the page to the right, 03244902. Mr. Cizmovic indicates to

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "There's no discord in Prijedor anymore." Karadzic: "Miskovic can do good work. Right?" Cizmovic: "Yes. Prijedor is resolved." And then further halfway down the page in English and at the bottom of your page in B/C/S, Mr. Krajisnik, Cizmovic: "I've talked to Bijeljina." Karadzic: "To who?" Cizmovic: "Bijeljina." Karadzic: "Uh-huh." Cizmovic: "They are prepared for full cooperation. It's the same case with Northern Bosnia. I've prepared a small questionnaire for all of them." Karadzic: "Uh-huh." Cizmovic: "What have they managed to do? How far circulate they come?" Karadzic: Mm." Cizmovic: "Are they prepared to implement the first level of the instructions? What are the problems? What do they need help with? I am even prepared to form a sort of team with your help, a team that would possibly give them professional help with anything they find problematic." So as we can see from this intercept, Mr. Krajisnik, between the first and second sessions of the Council of Ministers on January 11th and January 17th, 1992, Mr. Cizmovic was going to various municipalities to determine the extent to which they had implemented the first level of the Variant A and B instructions. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despite my best intentions, I cannot make the connection with the instructions because the autonomous regions have nothing to do with the instructions in peacetime. Maybe they did something quite outside of that. He did tour regions. I can tell you what he did in Prijedor, in Banja Luka. All of that has nothing to do with instructions. I do not dispute that that paper existed, but I can tell you what he did in those towns, in Prijedor and Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What he did when in Prijedor and Banja Luka? At this period of time?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a recurrent problem, namely that there were rifts on the municipal level even after the establishment of the republic. And there was constant talk about the new leaderships being always worse than the previous ones. Then they wanted to join this Krajina. I know exactly what he did in Banja Luka and in Prijedor -- or rather, not what he did but what was going on. He himself is from Banja Luka, Mr. Cizmovic, and he says he was touring regions here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, is it your position that you do or you don't know what he did in Prijedor and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he did. I know what happened, what was going on in Prijedor and Banja Luka and what it might have been about. He didn't report to me about his visits to Prijedor and Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, whatever else was going on in Prijedor and Banja Luka, it's clear that Mr. Cizmovic was going to various municipalities with his sort of questionnaire in an effort to ensure the implementation of the first level of the instructions. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, he toured regions. You see, it's written here that he toured regions, Northern Bosnia, and the rest. I don't know what polling papers he distributed, what questionnaires. I know he was in charge of autonomous regions, but what, if anything, he did outside of that, I don't know. I don't know if he had any instructions. He was not in charge of that. He was the official representative of the republic. He was no secret agent; that's what I think, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Tieger. Again, I'm very much trusting that -- let's stick as much as we can to facts rather than anything else. Mr. Krajisnik, are you aware of any document which contains instructions split up in a first level and other levels which was at that time a -- playing a role? You told us already that you're not aware of the A and B variant document. Is there any other document containing instructions divided in different levels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know of any other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any clear reference to any non-written instructions split up on two levels or more levels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then stay out of further speculations. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 68, Your Honours, where we'll find the minutes of the second session of the Council of Ministers held on 17 January 1992. That's P64, P65, Treanor 7, tab 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 5 of the English and also page 5 of the B/C/S, SA010905, which reflect at item 8 "the realisation of the conclusions reached at the first meeting of the ministerial council of the Assembly of the Serbian People of BH." "The ministerial council expressed the view that the conclusions of the first meeting of the council had been put into effect. More emphasis should be put on the intensification of the activities aimed at coordinating the work of the governments in all SAOs in which the most important task is that of Jovan Cizmovic." Now, again, at the first page of these minutes, Mr. Krajisnik, it reflects your attendance and Dr. Karadzic's attendance, among others. So it's correct then that by the time of the second meeting of the ministerial council, the conclusions from the first meeting had been put into effect, that is those conclusions were underway and progressing?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's written here. I suppose it's a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And that would include, as we discussed earlier, the defining of ethnic territory, the establishment of government organs in the territory, and the economic disempowerment of the current authorities in the socialist republic of BH?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was supposed to be included, but it was never finalised. That was Mr. Cizmovic's task, but it was not completed, which means that they drew the wrong conclusion here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you say "they drew the wrong conclusion," do I take that to mean you mean they hadn't -- the conclusions hadn't been fully perfected or completed by that time. That's your -- is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I drew the wrong conclusion; I said they drew the wrong conclusion here. They formulated the wrong conclusion because not all of the underlying activities had been completed, such as taking over power, et cetera, assuming ethnic territories, taking control, et cetera. Also, Mr. Prosecutor, the sixth point was important as well, and I would like to explain it for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, with -- you were given a great deal of time to explain a great many things. Unless this bears directly on the questions I'm asking, I prefer to move on to my next questions about the subject we're addressing now. So although I know you have an interest always in expanding answers, I'd like to stay focussed on the subject we've been addressing for the last session and pursuing now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, at the very end of the cross-examination, if important matters have been left out which are directly relevant for the questions put to you, you'll have an opportunity to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn next to tab 69. That's a conversation between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I go back for one second --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to this because otherwise it slips out of our minds. Mr. Krajisnik, when we earlier talked about what was the need of going to the municipalities and tell them what to do and -- one of your explanations was that the whole issue of the regions, once the state would have been declared, was -- there was no need for them anymore. Now I see in this point 8 we just looked at, that "more emphasis should be put on the intensification of the activities aimed at coordinating the work of the governments of all SAOs in which the most important task is that of Jovan Cizmovic." That's, at least at first eye, seems to contradict what you earlier explained that there would be no need anymore for this regionalisation and that that explained the portion of the telephone conversation about running around, telling what to do, on the issue that was -- I think it said delivered or something, what was issued yesterday evening. I have not in my mind anymore what the exact wordings were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Implement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, implement yesterday night or last night. You said: There was no need anymore, and that was part of your explanation. Here it, however, seems that even one asks for -- a more intensive approach of this matter. I have difficulties in reconciling the two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll explain. I spoke about the telephone conversation between Karadzic and me when I ask him: Why do we need that? And he said: Until the new year, until the proclamation of Republika Srpska. So his job would not be necessary anymore because it had to do with coordination. I objected to that new post. I said: Why do we need him? I was just explaining the telephone conversation between Karadzic and me, and Karadzic replied that he would be in that position only until the new year. Eventually it turned out differently. He continued after the new year as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, tab 68 contains a telephone conversation on January 22nd, 1992, between Mr. Cizmovic and Dr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Not 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, 69. Between Mr. Cizmovic and Dr. Karadzic, and that will need a new number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be put on the list prepared by Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, here, Mr. Krajisnik, we see Mr. Cizmovic and Dr. Karadzic talking about five days after the second session of the Council of Ministers. And if we turn quickly to page 5 of the document in English and pages 5109 and 5110, we see references to Mr. Cizmovic's contact with Doboj, Bijeljina, Birac, Romanija, Herzegovina. And then if we can turn to page 6 of the English and page 03245111 of your -- well, it actually begins 5110 and on to 5111 of your version.

utterances.speaker: MR. CIZMOVIC SAYS
utterances.text: "Because, we should not interpret all these movements that are going on here as some kind of a secession, or as some defections." Karadzic: "Yes, yes." Cizmovic: "They should be understood only as ..." And Karadzic says: "An alternative."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I think in order to guide Mr. Krajisnik, this starts at 5110, then we now are at the top of 5111, the alternative.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Cizmovic says: "... of a situation, in a need to react everything should be ready on stand-by ..." Karadzic: "So we could react within two hours." Cizmovic: "Correct." Karadzic: "That's right." Cizmovic: "We have formed a Crisis Staff tonight, which is to operate in such cases when we cannot gather anybody, so they can gather first." Karadzic: "Excellent." Cizmovic: "So, the thing is functioning. Because a purpose has to be fulfilled, and instruction has to be fulfilled." Karadzic: "Yes, I agree." Now, Mr. Krajisnik, does this reflect Mr. Cizmovic's efforts toward the intensification of the implementation of the conclusions of the first meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean ministerial council?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct. Sorry --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This is a completely different, separate meeting where Mr. Ivanovic attended. You see it here where the communities of municipalities of Krajina gathered. You see that from the text above, and they say: "Let's not treat this as secession. They even attacked Najdanovic over there." This is nothing to do with the conclusions of the ministerial council; it's just a session of the community or union of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And what about Mr. Cizmovic's continuing efforts with such places as Doboj, Bijeljina, Birac, Romanija, and Herzegovina? Isn't that a continuation of his effort to ensure the implementation of the ministerial council's conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Cizmovic was a Montenegrin and so was Mr. Karadzic, and he was a confidant of Mr. Karadzic and he kept him informed. You see, Milakovic and Janjic here, people who were making plans, all of them, for the secession of Bosnian Krajina. Those were not the conclusions of the ministerial council. You see that in the text above. It's all written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in the short period before the break, Mr. Krajisnik, I'm going to turn quickly to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps not so quickly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would it help you if you -- we would give you a few hours to find your next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm absolutely confident that as soon as we break it will be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Then you have the whole of the night to think it over, but it's really the next question you'd like to put to Mr. Krajisnik. We will adjourn, Mr. Krajisnik, but not until after I have instructed not to speak with anyone about the testimony already given or still to be given. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 10.00, same courtroom, and if you would allow me to add that I wish you a lot of strength tomorrow morning with the dentist because that's not what people like most in their lives, although perhaps it's a minor inconvenience. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 1st day of June, 2006, at 10.00 a.m.
